sources.title: ASML reports Q3 2026 results
facts_used: Q3 net sales EUR11.7bn, gross margin 57.5%, installed-base-management sales EUR3.3bn.
2026 sales guidance EUR44-45bn and gross margin around 56%.
Management says currently planned 2027 and 2028 supply will not fully meet customer demand and is investigating capacity beyond the previously communicated 30% increase for 2028.
Management attributes installed-base upside to productivity-upgrade demand.

sources.title: ASML reports Q4 2025/full-year 2025 results
facts_used: 2025 sales EUR32.7bn, gross margin 52.8%, year-end backlog EUR38.8bn.
Initial 2026 guidance was EUR34-39bn sales and 51-53% gross margin.
Management linked stronger medium-term capacity plans to customers' AI-demand expectations.

causal_map.driver: Customer capacity plans for leading-edge logic/DRAM exceed ASML's currently planned EUV/DUV supply through 2028.
causal_map.transmission: Scarce system capacity plus negotiated pricing and high-value installed-base productivity upgrades can raise revenue visibility and mix/margin durability without requiring unit demand to accelerate indefinitely.
causal_map.valuation_logic: If supply-constrained demand converts into accepted orders and deliveries while installed-base upgrades remain strong, medium-term cash-earnings visibility can remain structurally higher than a simple cyclical equipment-revenue model implies.
catalysts_for_validation_not_observation: Independent confirmation of order quality/cancellation protection and customer concentration.
Evidence that capacity expansion does not dilute gross margin through supplier or ramp costs.
Separation of price/mix effects from one-off quarterly timing.

active_disconfirmation: The thesis may simply restate already-visible AI capex optimism; public reporting explicitly notes valuation sensitivity if AI returns disappoint.
Customer interest in 2029-2030 orders is not equivalent to firm, non-cancellable demand; ASML itself warns that interest may not become orders and orders may be cancelled, delayed or pushed out.
Export controls, especially geographic restrictions, can impair shipment conversion even with backlog.
Expanding manufacturing and supplier capacity can increase fixed/ramp costs and could weaken the assumed margin transmission.
A supply constraint can cap recognized revenue; scarcity is not automatically incremental earnings if output cannot rise.
Customer capex plans are exposed to AI infrastructure economics, financing conditions and semiconductor cyclicality.
falsification: Demand visibility weakens materially through cancellations/push-outs or customer capex reductions before capacity is monetized.
Capacity expansion raises output but gross margin fails to retain the pricing/mix benefit after normalization.
Installed-base productivity-upgrade demand reverts materially, undermining the second earnings channel.
Export restrictions prevent conversion of economically meaningful portions of backlog/demand into shipments.
Independent validator finds the thesis is not causally distinct from a generic AI-capex continuation claim or is already fully represented in Legacy.
